editors_note: Good morning, Saad. Today laptop makers promise offline AI, universities put AI tutors to the test, and Islamabad's electric buses reach two new sectors. Enjoy your paper.

three_things.text: Laptop chipmakers say common AI assistant features will run offline next year.
Universities released a free test that checks AI tutors for wrong answers.
Islamabad's electric buses reach two more sectors from Monday.

items.headline: Chipmakers race to put AI accelerators inside everyday laptops
items.dek: Three vendors say on-device models will run without a cloud connection by next year.
items.summary: Several laptop chipmakers announced new processors with dedicated AI units this week. They say common assistant features, like summarising documents and transcribing calls, will run fully offline. Analysts expect prices to stay flat because the units replace older graphics blocks.
key_points: New chips include dedicated AI units
Assistant features are designed to work offline
Analysts expect laptop prices to stay flat
items.why_this: You follow Technology and read two hardware stories this week.

items.headline: Open-source browser adds built-in tracker blocking & <private> mode by default
items.dek: The change ships to all desktop users in the next stable release.
items.summary: An open-source browser project said its next release will block cross-site trackers by default and open new windows in a stricter private mode. The developers said page breakage was rare in testing.
key_points: Stricter private mode for new windows

items.headline: Smartphone makers agree on a common repair-parts portal
items.dek: Spare screens and batteries will be listed with prices in one place.
items.summary: A group of phone makers said they will publish spare-part prices and repair guides on a shared portal starting next quarter.

items.headline: Universities publish shared test to check AI tutors for wrong answers
items.dek: The benchmark covers maths, physics and chemistry at school level.
items.summary: A group of universities released a free benchmark that checks whether AI tutoring tools give correct and well-explained answers. Early results show large gaps between subjects.
key_points: Covers school-level maths, physics and chemistry
items.why_this: You love Artificial Intelligence and read AI stories for minutes at a time.

items.headline: Start-up shows small language model that runs on a phone in airplane mode
items.dek: The model is about a tenth of the size of popular assistants.
items.summary: A start-up demonstrated a compact language model running entirely on a mid-range phone. It handles notes and short emails but struggles with long documents.

items.headline: Coding assistants now explain their changes line by line
items.dek: Two popular developer tools added the feature after user requests.
items.summary: Two developer tools now show a short explanation next to each line they change, so programmers can review edits faster.
items.why_this: You follow Artificial Intelligence and Programming & Dev.

items.headline: Islamabad expands electric bus routes to two new sectors
items.dek: Officials say the routes start running from Monday morning.
items.summary: The capital's transport authority said electric bus service will reach two more sectors next week, with buses every 12 minutes at peak hours.

items.headline: State Bank keeps policy rate unchanged, cites steady inflation
items.dek: The decision was in line with most analyst forecasts.
items.summary: The central bank held its policy rate, saying inflation has been stable for three months. It said it would watch food prices closely.

items.headline: Astronomers spot a planet with a sky full of glass rain
items.dek: The finding comes from the same telescope that mapped its weather last year.
items.summary: Researchers say a hot gas giant far from Earth appears to have winds carrying silicate particles. They want more observations before confirming the weather model.
key_points: Hot gas giant with silicate clouds
items.why_this: Something new, outside your usual topics.

items.headline: Pakistan name unchanged squad for the second Test
items.summary: Selectors kept the same fifteen players after the first Test draw.
items.why_this: Matches your interest: pakistan cricket team.

items.headline: Football: late goal keeps leaders three points clear
items.summary: A stoppage-time header gave the league leaders a narrow home win.

items.headline: Game studio delays its open-world sequel to spring
items.summary: The studio said the extra months would go to performance fixes.
